items.summary: Better Perf TCO vs NVIDIA GB300, First Principles Physics-Based Architecture, High MFU and MBU, UBenchX, Low Latency, Alisa Liu vs Eileen Gu
items.story_key: story|title:aws challenger trainium3 inference and microarchitecture deep dive
items.content_excerpt: The Nvidia GPU was originally built to shade pixels, and every Nvidia generation since 2017 has bolted on another piece of AI-specific hardware to fix the bottleneck the previous one exposed. Volta added Tensor Cores, Hopper added TMA for tile data movement between HBM and SRAM, and Blackwell added Tensor Memory for accumulating. Nvidia removed many hardware units that are required to render graphics for their datacenter GPUs In comparison, the Trainium microarchitecture is built ground-up specifically for ML workloads, with tiles as a first-class primitive instead of having a sea of threads and then bolting on tensor/tile compute and data movement engines. Trainium3 behaves the way the physics says it should. In this past this meant software was a humongous challenge, but now no longer. 7 months later, Trainium 3 and TPUs are live on InferenceX , both trading blows or even winning vs Nvidia GB300 in cost to generate tokens at TCO. We will dive into those details below. This advantage is not purely due to Amazon’s ultra low cost supply chain. It's also due to microarchitectural decisions, which we will dive into in this post. For example, using the Trainium Descriptor Generation Engines (DGE), the equivalent of Nvidia TMA and AMD MI455X TDM, our microbenchmarks show that Trainium can reach peak HBM bandwidth utilization (MBU) at small message sizes, which is not possible on Nvidia GPUs. Furthermore, our testing covers cycle-level SRAM scratchpad latency and bandwidth testing (SBUF to PSUM), rack-scale bandwidth and latency microbenchmarks, attention exponential testing, and the precise cycle-level latency of different shapes, including how different attention head_dim (K) would affect the percentage of roofline. Every result comes from UBenchX, our microbenchmark suite, and we model each unit from first principles before we measure it. We thank Nafea Bshara (Co-Founder of AWS Annapurna Labs), Ron Diamant (Trainium Chief Architect), Michael Shteinbok, Armin Ebrahim and the rest of their team for helping teach us their architecture and validate our benchmark experiments. Star the InferenceX & UBenchX GitHub repository if you find the open-source benchmark and data useful ! InferenceX is the only inference benchmark in the world to have TPUv7, OpenAI Jalapeño, Nvidia Rubin NVL72, AMD, and now, Trainium3. AgentX measures Trainium3 on a production end-to-end agentic inference workload. This is achieved by replaying real coding-agent sessions against a Trainium3

items.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories. However, current paradigms are fragmented: pattern-transfer methods lack catalog-wide event memory, whereas online memory models suffer from endpoint-role asymmetry that degrades unseen-answer ranking. Furthermore, sparse early interactions exhibit both long-range dispersion and local redundancy under skewed distribution. To address these challenges, we propose INSPIRE (Integrating Shared Patterns and Individual Evidence for Reasoning), a two-stage forecasting framework over a known catalog. In Stage I, INSPIRE learns an availability-aware shared-pattern predictor that fuses event-updated memory across the full candidate catalog while applying coordinated query- and catalog-side masking. Subsequently, Stage II freezes this predictor and optimizes a lightweight individual-evidence adapter (EA) combining textual semantic priors with correlation-weighted long-range event statistics under support- and role-balanced co-answer supervision with prior-odds debiasing and soft residual alignment. In addition, we decompose evaluation by endpoint roles and track longitudinal emerging-answer cohorts via query-micro and answer-entity macro metrics. Across four benchmarks based on the ICEWS and GDELT event datasets, INSPIRE improves Emerging MRR by 16.73%-88.83% over the strongest baselines. Relative to paired Stage I predictors, EA further increases Emerging MRR by 8.28%-32.63%, Answer-new MRR by 7.81%-41.24%, and cohort macro MRR by 9.64%-39.94%, gains attributed to semantic priors and candidate-level score competition suppressing mismatched established competitors without zero-support prior shortcuts. The official code is publicly available at https://github.com/KcAcoZhang/INSPIRE.

items.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
items.story_key: story|title:swarms flocks gangs how to build train and evaluate multi agent systems
items.content_excerpt: This is an aspirational blog series for aspirational readers. We (us, the community, you) want to build our own agent swarms because they're exciting, challenging, and increasingly capable. Furthermore, it would be extremely cool if we could train our own agents to work in a swarm. And exponentially cool if those swarms used small and affordable models. That's what we'll do in this series! Each blog post will include some context on building swarms, alongside reproducible examples that you can run on Hugging Face Jobs. This post's example takes about five hours on two H200s, which costs roughly $50. Multi-Agent Systems are hard to get working. Adding agents changes the agent's context, the budget, and in turn the complexity of the whole system. Mixing agents' context together through communication is not an inherent performance boost compared to a single agent. The model needs to learn to communicate through training. How do we define what models should learn? And which model weights do we update when we're dealing with many agents? In this series, we'll work through those problems with an educational overview and practical examples. Each post will introduce a question, build a small system, and examine what happens and how you can reproduce it. This first example starts with four agents, a shared language model, and a simple verifiable task. It's ideal to implement yourself, to tinker with, and to learn from. We've heard a lot about swarms over the past few months, both good and bad. In September this year, OpenAI announced that a swarm of roughly 10,000 agents had found a singularity in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, one of the Millennium Prize problems. A smaller group of nearly 100 agents had already disproved regularity for the unforced 3D Euler equations, a closely related open problem. But swarms don't always work on the problems we want them to. METR's investigation of the Hugging Face incident found that around 1,200 OpenAI agents, which were supposed to be isolated, had found a way to exchange over 70,000 messages and files. Around 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face while looking for ways to fool their benchmark's scorer, without instruction to do so. A big swarm isn't, by itself, evidence that cooperation helped. Noam Brown estimates that less than 10% of the Navier-Stokes result came from multi-agent cooperation. items.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
items.summary: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. Existing benchmarks test compromised tool channels or adaptive multi-turn attacks, though they may not capture the unique capabilities of policy-governed tool-use agents, which must resist unauthorized requests without abandoning the legitimate work embedded in the same interaction. To fill this gap, we introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark built around scenario-specific stories, personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation. Each adversarial task targets an action explicitly prohibited by the policy provided to the assistant, while the policy remains hidden from the attacking user. TACT pairs each adversarial task with at least one benign counterpart, and its adversarial tasks retain authorized ground-truth actions when a compliant resolution remains available. We define these base tasks as TACT-Base. We additionally introduce TACT-TrustPrime, which places an independent benign task before an unrelated attack in the same conversation. We also propose Paired Selective Trustworthiness (PST), which combines explicit safe refusal with demonstrated capability on matched benign tasks, to analyze an agent's overcautiousness and practicality. Averaged across 6 different models as assistants, TACT-Base raises Attack-Induced Failure Rate (AFR) by 17.53% over four compatible attack baselines, and TACT-TrustPrime raises it by a further 17.01%. The two evaluated defense methods reduce AFR by only 8.35%--9.41% on average and do not consistently improve PST, underscoring the need for stronger policy-enforcement methods.

items.title: Why I'm Bullish on MCP for 2027
items.summary: Early MCP deserved its backlash. Code Mode, typed outputSchema, native multimodality, Agent Skills inside MCP, always-on MCP Events, and MCP Apps are turning it into the integration layer for agent harnesses in 2027.
items.story_key: story|title:why i m bullish on mcp for 2027
items.content_excerpt: MCP went through the full hype cycle in the last 18 months. Early excitement turned into backlash and confusion fast, with context bloat as the main complaint. When Skills arrived, most developers moved to CLIs and progressive disclosure instead. I never believed in that, and that sentiment is now changing. At Linear and Notion , agents now create roughly half of all issues (~2.4M/week) and pages, with Notion reporting 60x MCP traffic growth. At Atlassian , MCP handles over 5M tool calls per workday, and 44% of those users sit outside software teams where CLIs were never an option. At Neon , agent usage over MCP grows 14% week over week, and even Apple now ships local MCP servers for Pages, Numbers, and Keynote. The protocol is healthy and actively improving. The 2026-07-28 spec dropped stateful sessions and added official extensions, and clients are getting smarter about how they use them. Real tasks almost always take more than 1 tool call, e.g. you list open issues, grab details, check errors, and write a summary. With plain tool calling, every step needs another model turn and dumps information into the context. Joining data across 2 MCP servers uses the model's context as memory for intermediate payloads. Code Mode is changing how agents call MCP servers. Instead of putting 50 tool schemas into the prompt and calling 1 tool per turn, the harness gives the model a sandbox and exposes MCP tools as callable functions. It's already becoming the default in OpenCode 2.0, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi, and Factory Droid. Code Mode works best when the model knows what a tool returns before writing code. When an MCP server declares outputSchema alongside inputSchema , the client can generate typed stubs upfront and pass back structuredContent directly. The model chains multiple calls in 1 script, filters and joins in memory where compute is cheap, and returns only what matters. Compared to CLIs, MCP servers are natively multimodal. A tool call can return typed structuredContent for code alongside separate image, audio, or embedded resource blocks. Auth is also cleaner. CLIs and raw curl force you to store API keys on disk or in environment variables with broad permissions. An MCP client handles per-user OAuth 2.1 login flows and scoped tool permissions outside the sandbox, so connecting a remote SaaS product works without handing raw credentials to the agent. The debate of Skills plus a CLI versus MCP might come to an end as well. So far teams shipped CLIs or

items.title: vLLM Day-0 Support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview: Plugin Deployment and E2E Inference Acceleration
items.summary: vLLM supports Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview on day 0 through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin on the released vllm==0.32.0 wheel, with structure-aware kernel fusion, FlashIndexer, W4A8 QAT and DSpark speculative decoding.
items.story_key: model:vllm|ver:5.5|variant:flash,preview|title:vllm day 0 support for ernie 5 5 flash preview plugin deployment and e2e inferen
items.content_excerpt: The Baidu ERNIE team has worked with vLLM to bring day-0 support for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview to vLLM. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 280B total parameters and 14B activated per token. It supports a 1M-token context, thinks before it answers, and uses tool calling to carry out long-horizon Agent tasks. vLLM supports the model on release day through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin, a standalone package that you install into the same environment as the official vllm==0.32.0 wheel. Install the released vLLM wheel and the plugin into the same environment. vLLM discovers the plugin automatically through its vllm.general_plugins entrypoint, so there is nothing to import or configure. The following command serves the default FP4 weights on a single 4-GPU node, with DSpark speculative decoding drafting 7 tokens per step: To turn off thinking for a request, pass "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false} . Launch commands for 1M context, attention TP and PD disaggregation are in the vLLM-ERNIE README and the vLLM recipe . ERNIE 5.5 Flash was designed with inference cost as a primary goal from the start, weighing activated compute, KV cache size and long-context overhead together. Every component, from the attention structure and residual connections to the MoE layers and the output head, was redesigned around that goal. For design and training details, see the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview blog . ERNIE 5.5 Flash introduces several new structures in attention and MoE: low-rank cross-head post-mixing (VHA post-mix), Multi-Router Latent MoE, the MultiMax output head and sigmoid output gating. When implemented op by op from their mathematical definitions, these structures produce many intermediate tensors and pay for them in memory traffic and kernel launches. For each structure, we designed a dedicated fused kernel around its compute and memory-access profile, and folded everything that can be precomputed into the weights at load time. The fused kernels run 1.55× to 6.53× faster than naive implementations. Together, these fusions cover the full forward pass of ERNIE 5.5 Flash, from attention and MoE routing to the output head. They cut the number of kernel launches and the round trips of intermediate tensors through GPU memory while keeping the numerics aligned, and they underpin the model's high inference performance. The Baidu ERNIE inference team developed FlashIndexer, a lightweight indexer acceleration built on dynamic head routing

We are rolling out Genie 4 to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, offering more responsive, social, and interactive world generation. You can now use natural language to edit environments in real time, add native audio, and share your creations in our new community gallery. Visit the Project Genie website to start building your own worlds or join the waitlist if you are a Google AI Pro member. This update unlocks first-time access to Genie 4, new upgrades to Genie 3, the Project Genie agent which helps users build their vision, and a community gallery to discover, explore, and remix worlds. With Genie 4 , our most realistic and interactive world model yet, you can now prompt mid-session to change the world you created. items.title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
items.summary: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. This concern is salient in military settings, where autonomous weapons raise the possibility of delegating force decisions to software agents. In this work, we study whether a drone agent's action boundary is stable under changes to the target descriptor. We evaluate recent and popular LLMs in a simulated perception-action pipeline over real-world drone imagery, where models can localize requested targets and invoke a simulated lethal tool. We find two concerning failure modes. First, some LLM agents invoke the lethal tool for ordinary generic descriptors such as \emph{people}, requiring no jailbreak at all. Second, an agent that initially appears conservative under protected descriptors can become unsafe under a simple semantic target shift.

items.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
items.summary: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

items.title: claude-code v2.1.331
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
  • Added oidc.groups_jsonpath to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
  • Added an API connectivity section to claude doctor that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
  • Added a notice when tap-mode voice dictation stops by itself, after 15 seconds without recognized speech or at its 2-minute limit
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION to ask for uncompressed model responses behind a proxy that cuts compressed ones off; not advised yet for self-hosted runners or Remote Control
  • Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_IDP_CONNECT_BY_HOSTNAME=1 for Claude apps gateways: with oidc.use_proxy: true, sign-in requests hand the proxy an https IdP's hostname even with NO_PROXY set
  • Added gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.response.model and gen_ai.operation.name to claude_code.llm_request trace spans; gen_ai.usage.input_tokens includes prompt cache tokens
  • Added optionalDependencies to plugin manifests: plugins that install with the plugin listing them and can be disabled or uninstalled on their own
  • Fixed MCP tool calls hanging for up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server
  • Fixed PushNotification telling a headless run, such as a scheduled one, that the terminal was active in its first minute, instead of saying whether a mobile push was requested
  • Fixed /install-github-app skipping the repository step after setup warnings when no repository was found, and Esc not going back from its workflow list and sign-in steps
  • Fixed one-line tool results cut with no ellipsis in narrow windows, Markdown stars in the Auto mode tab of /permissions, and a hook's reason to stop a forked skill showing twice
  • Fixed /diff hiding its key hints and not selecting files in windows of 24 to 26 rows, and leaving out files added with git add -N in a repository with no commits
  • Fixed the first-run theme list showing too few themes in short windows, and /usage and other tall screens coming out garbled there
  • Fixed /bug in fullscreen hiding its Yes and No answers behind a long report, and Yes staying out of view in very short windows
  • Fixed /compact and auto-compact sometimes losing part of the conversation summary when the summary quoted certain XML tags
  • Fixed Claude not being told when permission rules on the Agent tool dropped its queued message to a subagent that had already ended
  • Fixed a Remote Control message sometimes showing above the reply that was finishing when it was sent
  • Fixed Stop hooks that read the transcript missing the last reply in Claude Desktop; SubagentStop hooks now wait for it too
  • Fixed turns and subagents failing in cloud sessions, or timing out on long replies elsewhere, when a reply went silent while Claude was still thinking; Claude Code now tries the request once more
  • Fixed Esc and Stop waiting about a minute or more when the contents of a cloud or network file that Claude is reading stall
  • Fixed Code Mode sessions resumed with --resume or --continue in another permission mode losing thinking and the prompt cache; one begun in a mode that asks keeps that mode's limits on scripts
  • Fixed Code Mode sending a request about every second when a ! or slash command was typed while a script was running
  • Fixed an interrupted or failed plugin update leaving a partial plugin folder that later loaded with skills or other components missing (#102186)
  • Windows: Fixed file writes on FAT32 and exFAT drives asking for permission every time in some plugin sessions
  • Fixed Claude failing to read a notebook that has a null output or an error output with no traceback
  • Fixed a rewind deleting files after a restore had failed
  • Fixed auto mode sometimes refusing Claude's call to stop a /loop, which left the next wake-up to fire
  • Fixed a Workflow agent's background shells and MCP servers sometimes being left running after it handed back its report
  • Windows: Fixed /desktop downloading the older Claude Desktop installer, and asking for an update when an older install's folder was left behind
  • Fixed claude plugin install, marketplace add and similar commands hanging with no output when managed settings needed an approval that could not be asked for
  • Fixed a permission rule on a subagent's model, such as Agent(model:*), blocking Claude's follow-up message to a subagent started on this version with no model named
  • Fixed PermissionRequest hooks not saving Skill(name:*) allow rules outside local settings
  • Fixed "Ask your admin" asking to raise your own limit when your team's pooled group budget blocked you, and saying "Request sent" when an admin had approved your request in the last few minutes
  • Fixed Code Mode losing the middle of a long script output; Claude now gets a path to the uncut text (#111373)
  • Fixed hold-to-talk dictation stopping early and losing words when Claude Code was busy
  • Fixed Code Mode with --bare not telling Claude what its scripts can call
  • Fixed a crash when a custom API endpoint returned a tool call with no tool name; the call now fails with an error and the session continues
  • Windows: Fixed a possible crash when the machine is almost out of memory
  • Fixed the CLI freezing on some replies, and quoted text sometimes going missing or showing twice
  • Windows: Fixed Claude Code refusing to start when managed settings in the registry contain non-ASCII characters such as Japanese (#93280)
  • Windows: Fixed Remote Control clients showing no steps for a new subagent
  • Fixed @-mentions written as @file#10-12 attaching the whole file instead of those lines
  • Fixed Claude misreading a pasted artifact invitation link; it now asks you to accept the invitation and paste the artifact's own link
  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands sometimes failing to start on a full temp disk, for sandboxes whose file rules keep commands out of the temp directory
  • Improved typing speed in screen reader mode, most of all in long sessions
  • Improved start-up time: a session started soon after another no longer waits for the model list, and one outside a git repository without .claude/settings.local.json no longer waits on git
  • Windows: Improved the speed of the first Bash command in a session on machines with no custom shell start-up files
  • Improved the plugin auto-update notice to name plugins it newly installs as dependencies, separately from updated plugins
  • Improved Code Mode tool search to show more of an MCP tool's description, with its limits, formats and defaults
  • Improved the Console sign-in link shown by /login and claude auth login --console: it is now much shorter
  • Improved Claude's list of your artifacts: it now marks web pages, so Claude is less likely to try opening one with the Claude Docs connector
  • Improved the folder trust prompts in short terminals: fullscreen /cd and /add-dir show their choices in fewer rows, and the prompt at launch keeps the folder path in view when it has many warnings
  • Changed the questions for stopping auto-connect in /ide and for /clear, /compact or /rewind in a subagent's view to list Yes first; they still start on No, so Down then Enter now answers No
  • Changed what a PermissionDenied hook's retry: true tells Claude: make the refused call again only if you asked for that call
  • Changed in a future release, on or after November 30, 2026: plugin marketplaces in managed extraKnownMarketplaces will auto-update by default. To opt one out, set "autoUpdate": false on its entry
  • Windows: Changed start-up with managed settings in the registry: check them before upgrading, as an HKLM policy outranks managed-settings.json and a broken value can stop the start
  • [VSCode] Added a warning and a link to the revoke page when you log out and the request to revoke your claude.ai login isn't confirmed
  • [VSCode] Added a notice before sending a very large selection or attached text file, and advice under "Prompt is too long" that names the large part and what to do next
  • [VSCode] Added "Add Cell to Chat" to the notebook cell menu, which attaches a cell with its outputs or error
  • [VSCode] Added "Fix with Claude Code" as a quick fix for errors and warnings and to failed tests in the test peek and the Test Results view, which puts the problem into the chat box
  • [VSCode] Added "Add to Chat" to the right-click menu of changed files in the Source Control view
  • [VSCode] Added "Resolve Merge Conflicts" to the editor title of a file with merge conflicts and to the Merge Changes group in Source Control
  • [VSCode] Fixed raw tags for selected code under a reworded prompt, the mode button flashing Manual, the slash menu hiding its highlighted row, a broken sign-in image, and a blinking Accept/Reject bar
  • [VSCode] Fixed a forked conversation overwriting the original conversation's plan file; a fork or rewind that can't copy the plan now shows a warning
  • [VSCode] Fixed voice dictation saying no speech was recognized when its connection closed or never opened; it now says the connection was lost or couldn't connect
  • [VSCode] Fixed an unsent side question being lost when its panel closes
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape stopping Claude after renaming a session, and typing going nowhere after closing the session history with Escape
  • [VSCode] Fixed Rename, Mark as Unread and Add to Group saying "still connecting" on a tab that resumed a session from its history
  • [VSCode] Fixed wide tables and long paths cut off, long errors hiding their close button, errors out of view in the Add MCP server form and Chrome dialog, and plugin pictures ignoring the editor theme
  • [VSCode] Fixed later prompts and the message box covering the Rewind code dialog, and focus jumping from "Never mind" to "Rewind" when it finishes checking files
  • [VSCode] Fixed the command menu keeping an earlier match highlighted while you type more in its filter, so Enter could run the wrong row
  • [VSCode] Fixed the @ menu showing "No files found" before its first search results arrived, or when it couldn't search all files of a very large workspace, which it now says
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape stopping Claude at a Remove or Delete confirmation in MCP, Hooks and Memory dialogs, on a side question panel's button or link, and on the Bookmarks button with its panel open
  • [VSCode] Fixed empty boxes showing instead of the + and − signs in diffs (#73069)
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat no longer following Claude's reply after the panel was resized, or hidden and shown again
  • [VSCode] Fixed a chat left in bypass permissions mode reopening in Auto mode instead of your initial permission mode when settings disable bypass
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat panel freezing on some CSS code blocks and diffs
  • [VSCode] Fixed the context usage indicator disappearing after an API error, "Prompt is too long", or a slash command
  • [VSCode] Fixed a message queued behind a queued /clear being lost
  • [VSCode] Fixed Manage Plugins losing its search box or showing no message when a search has no match, and not saying that the list of available plugins failed to load
  • [VSCode] Fixed proposed changes to notebooks and files with a custom editor opening in a tab with no Accept or Reject that stayed open after the answer
  • [VSCode] Fixed the spend limit message telling Team and Enterprise members to run /usage-credits, which can't send a request to their admin from the panel
  • [VSCode] Fixed a written message being wiped by Tab on a command in the "/" button's menu or by a click on an onboarding suggestion
  • [VSCode] Fixed Claude continuing to edit files after you rewind code while it is working
  • [VSCode] Fixed typed text being lost after /tasks, /copy, /export, a skipped /feedback, or /plan while already in plan mode
  • [VSCode] Fixed the question card dropping a typed "Other" answer on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, and sending the word "Other" when nothing was typed
  • [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing "Something went wrong" for a conversation in which a gateway sent a tool call with no name
  • [VSCode] Fixed unsaved changes being missed, and Claude's edit being overwritten by the next save, in a folder opened through a symlink
  • [VSCode] Fixed @-mentions attaching nothing, or another file of the same name, after Claude changed folders with cd
  • [VSCode] Fixed the arrow keys replacing typed text with an old prompt while selecting, and dropping edits to a recalled prompt
  • [VSCode] Fixed an @-mention added while a permission prompt was open being lost
  • [VSCode] Fixed shortcuts such as Ctrl+1, Alt+1 or Ctrl+Space answering an open dialog, which could restore files in the rewind confirmation or switch the git branch
  • [VSCode] Fixed prompts that start with a file path or code comment being sent without the selected code and having no fork or rewind menu
  • [VSCode] Fixed file links in the chat ignoring your editor associations for files in the workspace, except notebooks (#81482)
  • [VSCode] Fixed selected lines staying attached to your next message after their file's tab was closed
  • [VSCode] Fixed new sessions starting in Edit automatically after pressing Shift+Tab through it to reach Plan mode
  • [VSCode] Fixed an edited command on the permission prompt running without the line breaks that were typed or pasted into it
  • [VSCode] Fixed a newly opened Claude tab not focusing its message box, or taking the keyboard late from the terminal or command palette and sending the typed text as a prompt
  • [VSCode] Fixed Alt+K line ranges such as @app.ts#5-10 sending the whole file, or its first 2,000 lines, instead of the selected lines
  • [VSCode] Fixed diff tabs opening out of order when several subagents wait for approval, and a later edit to the same file cancelling an earlier one
  • [VSCode] Fixed Enter rewriting a message or running a menu action when a /word such as the path /api stands beside other text, and running a typed slash command without its arguments
  • [VSCode] Fixed Electron apps and extension tests failing to start from Claude, a hook or an MCP server; a wrapper, hook or server that runs VS Code as Node must now set ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1
  • [VSCode] Fixed Claude not being told when you reject part of a proposed edit or change it in the diff view before accepting
  • [VSCode] Fixed Escape on a permission prompt sending a half-typed instruction to Claude instead of cancelling
  • [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+J and Ctrl+O in the chat also opening VS Code's terminal or Open File dialog on Windows and Linux
  • [VSCode] Fixed the @ menu inserting the wrong file on a quick Tab or Enter, and Enter not sending a prompt that ends in an @word with no matching file
  • [VSCode] Fixed new Claude tabs staying blank and the side bar failing to load after closing a tab while Claude was still starting
  • [VSCode] Fixed a quick double click in the panel pressing a button or row that appeared after the first click, or starting a second compaction from the context usage circle
  • [VSCode] Fixed switching models failing with "Settings file is not valid JSON" when settings.json is empty or starts with a byte order mark
  • [VSCode] Fixed memory growing with each fork or rewind of a long conversation until the window was reloaded
  • [VSCode] Fixed plan comments not showing on the plan approval card in Focus view
  • [VSCode] Fixed file links without a line number moving the cursor of an open file to line 1
  • [VSCode] Fixed a missing notification when a conversation running behind another one in the same panel needs a permission or an answer
  • [VSCode] Fixed Manage Plugins not loading when Claude Code is slow to start or fails to start, so a plugin that blocks startup can be turned off
  • [VSCode] Fixed proposed diffs showing and saving garbled non-ASCII text when files.encoding is not UTF-8
  • [VSCode] Fixed approved edits and writes saving right-to-left marks as literal \u200F escapes on lines with Hebrew, Arabic or Persian text
  • [VSCode] Fixed a model pick being ignored for the next message when Claude's process had ended or was still starting
  • [VSCode] Fixed Rewind showing "No active session" after Claude's process had ended
  • [VSCode] Fixed typing @ leaving a helper process running per tab when no browser is connected, except when Claude in Chrome's service can't be reached
  • [VSCode] Fixed the session list opening every transcript at once, which stalled the editor's extensions and could leave sessions out in projects with many sessions
  • [VSCode] Improved the time to the first reply in a new folder when the Python extension is installed and the folder has no Python
  • [VSCode] Improved the sign-in screen to say when it opened because a request was refused
  • [VSCode] Improved the speed of opening, restoring and switching back to long conversations, most of all with many file edits or where git is slow
  • [VSCode] Improved responsiveness in long chats: smooth typing and large file writes while a reply streams, faster permission prompts, and far less freezing on send with accessibility support on
  • [VSCode] Improved startup and memory use: the panel and new chat tabs open faster, a first message in a new tab is answered sooner, and on Pro and Max plans the folder trust dialog comes up sooner
  • [VSCode] Improved speed in remote windows (SSH, WSL, containers): the panel starts, replies appear and sessions reopen faster
  • [VSCode] Improved the time to a response for the first message after a chat has been idle for a few minutes on a machine that is low on memory
  • [VSCode] Improved how fast chats start, open from history and come back after a restart on slow or antivirus-scanned disks
  • [VSCode] Improved how fast diffs appear in reopened conversations, and removed diff menu entries that did not work
  • [VSCode] Improved the @ file menu to list the files of open editor tabs first, the most recently used on top
  • [VSCode] Changed saving a proposed diff to accept it only after you click or type in its proposed (right) side; a notification says when a save is refused or a close with Save applies nothing
  • [VSCode] Changed diffs from a terminal session to open without moving keyboard focus, and beside a file with unsaved changes; to answer, click Accept or use the terminal
  • [VSCode] Changed permission cards to show only Yes and No when allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly is set and the card would offer an allow rule; key 2 on those cards now answers No
  • [VSCode] Changed a Claude tab to ignore Enter and show a notice when its Find box has lost the keyboard
release_highlights: Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
Added oidc.groups_jsonpath to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
Added an API connectivity section to claude doctor that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
